name: 135 mm f/1.8 (patent example, Sony telephoto with floating focus)
representativeSource: photonstophotos.net Optical Bench Hub row "WO2019-187633 Example01P Sony FE 135mm F1.8 GM", https://www.photonstophotos.net/GeneralTopics/Lenses/OpticalBench/OpticalBenchHub.htm, accessed 9/28/2026. Corroborated structurally: our transcription of Numerical Example 1 has 13 elements in 10 air-spaced groups, matching the DPReview specifications page's "Elements: 13, Groups: 10" for SEL135F18GM.

source.ref: WO 2019/187633 A1, Table 1 / First Embodiment ("第1の実施の形態", 数値実施例1)
source.location: Table 1 (surface data), Table 2 (asphere, surface 9), Table 3 (f/Fno/omega/Y/L), Table 4 (variable gaps) of the published PDF (patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/.../WO2019187633A1.pdf; the Google Patents HTML page renders these five tables as scanned images, not machine-readable text, so we transcribed from the PDF page images directly)

asph.convention: patent prints kappa directly (kappa=0 here means no added conic term), and labels the polynomial terms A, B, C, D for the 4th/6th/8th/10th order coefficients in that order; mapped here to A4=A, A6=B, A8=C, A10=D

surfaces.label: L5 (asph, front focus group GR1 rear element)
aperture stop S; gap d3 (stop to GR3)

gaps.note: index 9 = patent surface 10 (d1, GR1-GR2 gap); GR2 is the first focus group, moving object-to-image side on focusing closer. closeObjectDistance is the patent's d0 at magnification -0.25 (its closest tabulated condition), measured from surface 1.
index 14 = patent surface 15 (d2, GR2-stop gap); moves with GR2.
index 15 = patent surface 16, the stop itself (d3, stop-GR3 gap); GR3 is the second focus group, moving image-to-object side.
index 18 = patent surface 19 (d4, GR3-GR4 gap); moves with GR3. GR4 and the filter/image distance are fixed.

focus.minFocusSource: DPReview specifications page for the Sony FE 135mm F1.8 GM, https://www.dpreview.com/products/sony/lenses/sony_fe_135_1p8_gm/specifications, accessed 9/28/2026 ("Minimum focus: 0.7 m"); sony.com/electronics.sony.com would not load for us, so we cite DPReview's reproduction of Sony's own published spec sheet rather than Sony's own page directly (see research notes).

iris.source: DPReview specifications page for the Sony FE 135mm F1.8 GM, https://www.dpreview.com/products/sony/lenses/sony_fe_135_1p8_gm/specifications, accessed 9/28/2026 ("Number of diaphragm blades: 11")

notes: This patent's HTML page on Google Patents renders Tables 1-27 (surface data, aspheric coefficients, overall specs, variable gaps, group focal lengths, x5 embodiments) as scanned page images (JPOXMLDOC01-appb-T0000xx.png), not OCR text, and the WO/PCT PDF itself has no text layer at all (confirmed: pypdf/pymupdf extract zero characters from all 90 pages). We transcribed Tables 1-4 for Numerical Example 1 directly from those table-image PNGs (fetched from patentimages.storage.googleapis.com, linked from the same Google Patents page) by reading the rendered image.
Filter FL (patent surfaces 25-26) is listed as two explicit surfaces per the schema convention, rather than folded into the last glass element's BF.
Single aspheric surface at patent surface 9 (rear-most element of the front group GR1); patent's own coefficient labels are A/B/C/D rather than A4/A6/A8/A10, mapped 1:1 in that order.
Patent gives no effective-diameter column; all `sd` values are our own paraxial-trace estimates.

stated.f = 130.950mm in the raw patent example vs. the 135mm marketed class; this generic-example vs shipped-product gap is normal for patent numerical examples and is called out per BRIEF.md's 'representative designs are schematic' guidance.

stated.bf (1.0000mm) is Table 1's own last-row thickness (filter rear to image), given as a plain number, not a symbolic 'BF'; Table 3 (overall specs) names no separate BF variable at all for this design. It is NOT the traditional full back focal distance, which would also include the 17.8946mm rear-element-to-filter air gap and the 2.5mm filter thickness (~21.39mm total); we check the self-check trace against the last surface's own tabulated 1.0000mm for consistency with how every other lens here is checked.
